beats.narration: They tuned out the atrocities because it was easier. Werner tried to do it, but Marie Lord lived in physical darkness.
And because she rigorously attended to the truth of her environment, she saw the world with perfect clarity. So the ultimate weapon is not the incendiary bomb.
It is the frequency we choose to listen to, the stories we choose to believe, and the knowledge we either hoard for ourselves or broadcast to save others.
The transmission of knowledge is the eternal battlefield. And our perception of it dictates our morality.
I want to leave you, the listener, with a thought to mull over long after this deep dive ends. Doer beautifully extrapolates this
idea to the modern day at the very end of the novel. Look around your physical space right now. Just look around. You are swimming in an ocean of invisible waves.
Wi-Fi networks, cell towers, targeted advertising algorithms, millions of texts and emails and data points flying invisibly through the air around your head.
Are you passively letting these frequencies wash over you? Walking on autopilot like the cited people in Paris? Who is controlling the transmitter in your life?
